lines.narration: When doctors sew you up, the most important thread never surfaces.
Forget the shoelace picture: loops and knots on top.
For scars that heal flat, the thread rides under the surface.
It's the subcuticular stitch: one thread hidden inside the skin.
The needle zigzags through one layer, catching both edges every pass.
Each pass pulls the gap shut: a zipper under the surface.
The end knot gets buried, where your skin swallows it whole.
No stitch tracks. Just a clean seam.
The thread dissolves on its own. No removal visit.
In about two days, the surface seals itself.
The best-stitched skin shows almost no trace.
The finest seam is the one you never see.
